clue.text: Writer Jane — typical American — penning principally erotic fiction

first letter
F is a standard abbreviation for fiction

explanation.surface: A reader describes Jane, an ordinary American woman, writing racy novels.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'Jane — typical American' look like a character sketch; together the words clue Jane Doe, the anonymous everywoman of American legal usage. E and F go inside DOE to give DEFOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English novelist and journalist who wrote Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders.

clue.text: Centre of military operations in theatre of war?

first letters of the three words

first and last letters

clue.text: Panama hat, mag and his sandwiches…a peaceful chap

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between slices, so the letters sit inside the words

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: A list of a man's belongings: a Panama hat, a magazine and his sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like part of his packed lunch; it is the verb, holding the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian independence leader championed non-violent resistance, so he was a man of peace.

clue.text: Foolish, sick arbitrator, ultimately good

blocks.note: ill means sick
a judge arbitrates
last letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately good' reads as 'it all worked out'; it asks only for the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision made with poor judgement is unwise or foolish, lacking good sense.

clue.text: Register Nick held with both hands

indicators.note: whatever is held is gripped from either side, so it ends up enclosed

blocks.note: to nick is to edge past or win narrowly, as in edging a vote

explanation.surface: A police register records a suspect being held with both hands cuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' suggests arrest (the nick is British slang for a police station); here it is a verb meaning to edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger is a book of accounts or records, so it is a register of entries.

clue.text: Chronic weak person eschewing R&B

R and B, as in the music genre rhythm and blues

explanation.surface: A lifelong wimp refuses to listen to rhythm and blues.
explanation.walkthrough: One R and the B are removed from the spineless creature; the answer's own R stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Inveterate means long-established and deep-rooted, like a chronic habit or condition that persists.

clue.text: Healthy appetite by the end of day

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: lust is a strong appetite or desire
last letter

explanation.surface: Someone in good health is hungry by evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' is a link here, meaning next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means vigorous and full of energy, so strong and in robust good health.
